Prevention: Inspect plant material for new plantations to check that they are free of snails.
Remove any objects or equipment that are not being used as traps and can serve as shelters (fallen fruits, pots, boxes, poles, etc.)
Within the plantation and surroundings, control plants that can serve as shelters or food (weeds, ivy, watercress or succulent plants) and remove crop residues.
Avoid excessive watering and use a drip system.
Try to water early in the day, not in the afternoon or evening.
Place physical barriers between plots, poles and plants.
Use copper foils or plastic bags and suspend them on poles without them touching the ground.
Encourage the presence of ground beetles, birds and mammals by avoiding the use of chemicals.
Monitoring: Monitor the adult snails in moist and shaded sites, such as near drains.
Look under rocks, on leaves and on crop residues for eggs, which look like tiny pearls.
Place traps (deep plastic containers with vertical sides at ground level) containing a bait:
Examples of bait: 1 tablespoon of yeast, 1 tablespoon of flour, 1 tablespoon of sugar and 1 cup of water, or, alternatively, use a small amount of beer.
Verify the traps every day until the population decreases.
Place the traps every 20 meters squared.
When snails are observed in traps (2-4 in 20 traps) or a trail of slime or irregular holes in leaves are observed, apply control measures.
Direct Control: Diurnal hand picking: use one of the following two traps every morning until the population decreases.
Crush snails or collect them in a bag and kill them at the end of the week (see note below).
Put traps (pieces of wood or plastic containers) with bait or beer on the soil.
Collect 1 kg of fresh papaya leaves or cassava peels (or a mix).
In the afternoon, put the pile of leaves away from the crop to protect it.
Change the leaves when they shrivel and dry.
Nocturnal hand picking: with a flashlight, collect adults or kill with a stick every other night until it is difficult to find them.
Then, continue the hand picking once a week.
Kill the adults in a bag with salt, burn or drown them in soapy water and bury the dead adults at least 10 cm deep.
When hand picking, always wear gloves and throw them away after use.
Don’t let children hand pick the snails as the snails can transmit parasites.
